w10_T4_005580: Marco started his school fundraiser with 119 dollars. In the morning, three student groups brought in 65, 61, and 42 dollars respectively. By afternoon, he had collected enough to multiply his total by 8 as a bank matched the funds. He then divided the matched amount into 4 equal parts for different school programs. What was the final amount in each part?
w10_T4_005590: Sarah had 211 dollars in her savings account. She withdrew 63 dollars for a new backpack. The next day, her parents gave her double the remaining amount. She then received another payment of 63 dollars from a summer job, and her aunt matched that amount five times over. His brother had collected 45 dollars (which was never used). How much money does Sarah have now?
w10_T4_005600: Two swimmers, Alex and Riley, are tracking their practice hours. Alex started with 225 hours logged. He added 33 more hours, then the training program tripled his total for certification purposes. The coach reduced his recorded hours by 807 to account for administrative errors, then doubled the amount for final record-keeping, and added 19 hours for a bonus session. By comparison, Riley has been swimming for exactly what final hour count did Alex end up with?
w10_T4_005601: Emma had collected 222 trading cards over the summer. She doubled her collection by trading with friends. Then she gave away 264 cards at school, lost 24 cards at the park, and sold 111 cards online. Tracking her remaining collection throughout this journey, how many cards did Emma have at the end?
w10_T4_005603: In the morning, a farmer had 62 chickens. By afternoon, 19 chickens had wandered off. Then 16 more were moved to another pen. The remaining flock was multiplied by 6 for a breeding program count, then multiplied by 9 for insurance purposes. Finally, 665 chickens were subtracted from the record (a correction for a counting error). What was the final number on the inventory?
w10_T4_005605: During a school day, the gym had 113 students. In the morning, 9 left for a field trip. By mid-day, 11 had returned from another activity. Then 24 students went to lunch, but 40 came back afterwards. Finally, 41 students left for home period. Tracking through the entire day, how many students remained?
w10_T4_005620: A bakery started with 41 cookies in stock. The morning rush resulted in 39 being sold, then 1 more was given away as a sample. By afternoon, 24 fresh cookies were baked. Before closing, 24 cookies were donated to the shelter. The bakery measured everything in dozens (a traditional unit). How many cookies did the bakery have left?
w10_T4_005623: Sarah started her day with 32 bookmarks. By morning, she gave away 24 to friends at school. Then she lent 2 to her classmates. At home, she created triple the remaining amount for a craft project. Finally, she used 10 of them as gifts for her cousins. Marcus has collected twice as many, but how many did Sarah end up with?
w10_T4_005626: A warehouse received 192 boxes of supplies. An incoming shipment added 13 more boxes. These were arranged into 6 separate storage sections. Each section was multiplied by 4 for a full inventory count. Then they were converted into dozens (units of measurement). How many total units were there after this conversion?
w10_T4_005627: A coffee shop served 81 customers in the morning. In the afternoon, 14 more customers arrived, and later 39 additional patrons came for evening service. The manager then grouped them by 6 for a study on peak hours. This group count was divided by 4 for scheduling purposes. Finally, 92 customers were subtracted from the projection (an adjustment for cancellations). What was the final customer projection?
w10_T4_005628: A bookstore had 146 novels in stock. On Monday, 69 were sold. The remaining books were doubled for a new shipment that arrived. Then 10 more books came in, followed by 3 others, and 57 used books were added to the inventory. The entire collection was tripled for a sale promotion. What was the final number of books in stock?
w10_T4_005629: Maya started her study session with 216 flashcards. She removed 192 to focus on difficult topics. By afternoon, 20 were added back, and another 6 were included from a friend. Then she lost 41 cards on the way home. Marcus had accumulated just a few, but how many flashcards did Maya have remaining?
w10_T4_005631: A factory produced 201 widgets. After quality checks, 36 were discarded. The remaining good widgets were sent to 9 different warehouses (9 times the quantity). Each warehouse received the same amount. Then 16 defective widgets were added for rework. The total count was multiplied by 8 for monthly reporting. Converting to hundreds, what was the final tally?
w10_T4_005635: A printer received 184 pages of orders. The order count was multiplied by 5 for a rush job. These were then divided by 4 to determine batch sizes. Each batch was tripled for reprinting purposes. Then everything was multiplied by 7 for archival records. Additionally, 33 pages were damaged (not used in calculations). How many archival pages were recorded?
w10_T4_005637: During the morning shift, a factory had 173 workers. This was tripled for a special project. Then 50 more were assigned. The workforce was multiplied by 5 for a shift rotation. The total was divided by 5 (returning to original scope). Then 541 worker-hours were subtracted from the payroll budget. What was the final adjusted workforce count?
w10_T4_005644: A sports team started with 95 players. The coach removed 59 for rule violations. Then 31 were benched for performance issues. Only 3 remained unavailable after these deductions. The remaining available players were multiplied by 6 for a statistical report. The report measured time in minutes per player (a unit conversion). What was the final statistical total?
w10_T4_005657: During a fundraiser, the group had 113 participants. Early on, 69 left due to weather. Then 18 returned when it cleared. By afternoon, 30 more left to catch trains. Later, 14 additional participants left early. However, 78 new volunteers arrived to help. Finally, 73 were subtracted from the final count for administrative purposes. Additionally, a competing group had collected 55 funds (not relevant). What was the final participant count?
w10_T4_005659: Two managers, Alex and Sam, track inventory. Starting with 216 items, Alex removed 85 damaged goods. Then 39 were marked as returns. Later, 81 items were discontinued. He then received 21 new items. The updated count was multiplied by 4 and then increased by 43 for accounting adjustments. Measured in currency conversion (dollars to cents), what was Alex's final inventory?
w10_T4_005667: Lisa and Tom are comparing their savings. Lisa had 132 dollars and received 56 more from babysitting. She earned another 56 from tutoring, and her grandmother gave her 36 dollars. From this total, she spent 107 dollars on equipment. Throughout these changes, how many dollars does Lisa have?
w10_T4_005668: Two entrepreneurs, Dana and Jordan, track profits. Jordan started with 239 dollars. She multiplied by 5 through initial sales. Then she earned 69 more. Her total was multiplied by 9 for expansion funding. She gained 69 additional dollars. Dana had started with a different amount, but how much profit did Jordan end with?
w10_T4_005669: Miguel and his sister Elena track their chores. Miguel began with 29 chore tasks. He completed 7 of them, earning money that was multiplied by 7. He then removed 19 tasks as delegated. He added 57 new tasks for the week. Finally, 8 were canceled. In minutes per task (a unit measurement), what was Miguel's final task count?
w10_T4_005677: A contractor started with 40 hours of work on a project. He multiplied this by 4 for a larger estimate. Then he subtracted 112 hours that were already completed. The remaining hours were multiplied by 9 in the morning for scheduling. Then multiplied by 9 again in the afternoon for extended planning. Finally, 51 hours were added as contingency time. What was the final scheduled hours?
w10_T4_005682: A company processed 227 orders. By the end of the day, 218 had been shipped. They then received 78 new orders. This amount was tripled for a weekly projection. After review, 210 orders were subtracted due to cancellations. Then 14 were added as rush orders. The final count was multiplied by 4 for inventory purposes. Additionally, 35 orders were pending (not included). How many orders were in final inventory?
w10_T4_005686: Two colleagues, Ben and Kate, split workload. Ben started with 24 tasks. He divided them in half to share equally. He then multiplied his share by 5. He added 11 more tasks. Then 48 were removed from his list. He doubled his remaining tasks by 9 for a projected month. Finally, he added 58 backup tasks. In hours per task (time conversion), what was Ben's final task total?
w10_T4_005688: Emma planted 43 tomato seeds in the morning. She multiplied this by 8 as a secondary planting in the afternoon. She added 3 more seeds she found. Then 50 seeds were removed due to quality issues. By evening, 23 seeds were added as a bonus from a neighbor. Tracking through the entire day, how many seeds did Emma have to plant?
